newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Uniserv ups volumes after courier alliance.
newsitem.headline: Uniserv ups volumes after courier alliance.

text.p: Shares in South Africa's United Service Technologies Ltd (Uniserv), which does business as Sun Couriers, on Friday morning saw large turnover on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange in a foreign buy deal.

Activity in the usually thinly-traded share follows news this week that Sun Couriers and fellow courier firm DHL International had set up a South African alliance to cover both domestic and international package delivery markets.
Dealers said 2.1 million Uniserv shares worth around 18.0 million rand had traded in a foreign purchase deal, where a local investor buys shares from offshore.
But dealers said that the large block of shares had changed hands at 825 cents, a large 115 cent discount to the ruling price of 940 cents where the share was last bid.
Brokerage Fleming Martin who carried out the deal confirmed the trade but gave no further details.
The DHL deal, which took effect on July 1, comes as United Parcel Service is establishing its own operation in South Africa after ending a long-standing partnership with Sun.

Under the new alliance, DHL will continue its own services in South Africa using its own offices, but Sun will act as delivery partner for DHL shipments destined for other locations in the 450 town Sun Courier domestic network.
Uniserv also runs a forwarding agent business under the name Union Transport.
